concepts.title: Human Development and Family Studies as a Discipline
concepts.definition: HDFS studies the changes people undergo from birth to old age and trains professionals to serve persons of different ages, needs and circumstances, treating home and workplace with equal respect.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- one discipline serving the whole life span
concepts.key_idea: Colleges rename the field Child Development, Human Development and Childhood Studies or Human Ecology, differing in emphasis but not in substance.
question_patterns: what is the discipline of human development and family studies
under which different names is HDFS taught at the college level
why does a career in HDFS demand honest self reflection
name the four major areas of work within HDFS
how does studying HDFS help in daily life

solution_steps.action: define the discipline and its breadth
solution_steps.explain: development across the life span plus service to individuals, families and groups
early childhood care and education, guidance and counselling, special education and support services, management of programmes for children, youth and elderly

worked_examples.q: Which discipline studies changes from birth to old age: HDFS or geology?

concepts.title: Attachment and Recognition in Infancy
concepts.definition: Babies bind themselves to the mother and other close carers, show fear of unknown faces around eight to twelve months, cry when the caregiver leaves and trail after her -- behaviour that fades as the toddler grasps that an absent mother has not vanished.
concepts.formula: sequence -- recognition to attachment to separation protest to security
concepts.key_idea: Stranger fear is a milestone, not a mischief: it proves the baby can tell familiar from unfamiliar faces.
question_patterns: what does a baby's fear of unknown people at 8 to 12 months indicate
describe how attachment to the primary caregiver shows itself in the first year
why does a one year old cry when the mother leaves the room
how does the child develop a sense of security about the caregiver's absence
which developments in the second year reduce clinging behaviour

solution_steps.explain: recognition of faces, fear of strangers, protest at separation, then restored security
each sign marks a growing cognitive and emotional capacity, not mere naughtiness

worked_examples.q: Around what age does fear of unknown faces appear: eight to twelve months, or eight years?

concepts.title: Substitute Care: Creche and Day Care
concepts.definition: When the mother works outside, another woman of the household, a neighbourhood home creche or an institutional centre can stand in; a creche formally designates an institution built for infants and young children away from home care, while day care covers preschoolers as well.
concepts.formula: care ladder -- family member to home creche to institutional centre
concepts.key_idea: Substitute care frees an older sibling for school and brings nutrition and health inputs to disadvantaged children.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe106.txt, substitute care and institutional care paragraphs (approx lines 110-201, 228-237)
question_patterns: what is a creche and which children does it serve
how does day care differ from a creche
why do working mothers need substitute care arrangements
how does institutional care help the older school going sibling
which extra services besides supervision may a care centre deliver

solution_steps.explain: creche for infants and young children, day care reaching into the preschool years
release of the older child for schooling plus nutrition and health interventions

worked_examples.q: Which institution is formally built for infants away from home care: a creche or a cinema?

concepts.title: Objectives of ECCE
concepts.definition: Early childhood care and education aims at the all round development of the child so full potential unfolds, readies the child for school, and stands behind women and children as a support service.
concepts.formula: three aims -- holistic development plus school readiness plus support to women and children
concepts.key_idea: Preschool complements, never replaces, the learning that happens naturally at home.
question_patterns: state the objectives of ECCE according to the NCF 2005 position paper
what is meant by holistic development of the child
how does preschool prepare a child for formal schooling
in what way is ECCE a support service for women
do children who never attend nursery school fail to learn

solution_steps.explain: development of potential, preparation for school, support services
all children learn naturally; preschool widens exposure and smooths the path to formal school

worked_examples.q: ECCE aims at all-round development so the child's full what unfolds: potential or wardrobe?

concepts.title: Guiding Principles of ECCE
concepts.definition: ECCE practice rests on play as the engine of learning, art as the base of education, respect for the special texture of children's thinking, lived experience over rote expertise, a mix of formal and informal exchanges, local materials and cultures, developmentally apt flexibility, and attention to health and well being.
concepts.formula: principle set -- play plus art plus experience plus locality plus flexibility plus health
concepts.key_idea: Routines should mix the familiar with gentle challenge, so curiosity survives and anxiety stays away.
question_patterns: list the guiding principles of ECCE given in NCF 2005
why is play treated as the basis for learning
what does primacy of experience rather than expertise mean
how do local materials and arts enter the preschool curriculum
what is meant by developmentally appropriate practices
why should familiar routines carry an element of challenge

solution_steps.explain: nine headings from play through health, well being and healthy habits
play way learning through leaves and stones; local folk art linking school to home

worked_examples.q: What does ECCE rest on as the engine of learning: play or drilling?

concepts.title: Age Stages: Infancy, Toddler, Preschool Child
concepts.definition: Early childhood stretches from birth to eight years, split at three; infancy covers the first year or two of total dependence; the two to three year old is a toddler whose walk still jumps; and the preschool child, ready for company beyond the family, may attend a Montessori school or an anganwadi under ICDS.
concepts.formula: stage bands -- infancy to 1 or 2 years, toddler 2 to 3, preschool 3 to 6, early childhood to 8
concepts.key_idea: Different stages need differently trained adults: infant care and preschool teaching are distinct skill sets.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe106.txt, Basic concepts stage definitions (approx lines 214-255)
question_patterns: define early childhood and state how it is divided
what is meant by infancy and till what age does it run
why is a two year old called a toddler
what is a preschool child and why is the stage named so
which schools follow the principles of Maria Montessori

which stage falls between 3 and 8 years of age

solution_steps.action: define each stage with its age band
solution_steps.explain: infancy, toddler, preschool, and the umbrella early childhood phase
Montessori schools and anganwadis under ICDS serve the preschool band

worked_examples.q: Early childhood stretches from birth to what age: eight or eighteen?

concepts.title: Child Centred Approach and the Play Way Method
concepts.definition: A good preschool runs on the child centred, play way route: learning arrives through enjoyable activity among peers, the setting stays safe, loving and rich in people and play material, and no child is forced into desk bound lessons that wither curiosity.
concepts.formula: method -- enjoyment plus peers plus caring adult plus play material, without formal drill
concepts.key_idea: Children eat by themselves and try new foods among peers; the right setting teaches what nagging cannot.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe106.txt, learning environment and preschool benefits (approx lines 130-181)
question_patterns: what is meant by a child centred approach
why is the play way method suited to young children
describe the features of an optimal learning environment for a three year old
what happens when a young child is forced to sit and learn like an older pupil
how do peers speed up a child's learning in preschool
which benefits does a good preschool bring to children in difficult circumstances

solution_steps.explain: the child's curiosity and pace drive the activity, the adult only arranges conditions
forced seat work breeds anxiety and kills the questioning habit

worked_examples.q: Learning through enjoyable activity among peers is which method: play way or lecture way?

concepts.title: Piaget and Vygotsky for the ECCE Teacher
concepts.section: Basic concepts and Preparing for a Career
concepts.definition: Piaget showed that young children understand the world in ways of their own and must explore at their own pace, while Vygotsky stressed how much a concerned, knowledgeable adult matters; together they set the teacher's task -- know what the child can do and pitch every activity neither too easy nor too hard.
concepts.formula: task difficulty -- below interest threshold plus above frustration threshold, both avoided
concepts.key_idea: The preschool educator must know the child's capabilities more than facts about the world.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe106.txt, Piaget and Vygotsky passages (approx lines 257-265, 376-389)
question_patterns: what did Piaget conclude about the way young children understand the world
why do young children need a supportive environment to explore
which need did Vygotsky highlight for preschool education
why must tasks given to a child be neither too easy nor too difficult
how should a teacher use knowledge of the child's capabilities

solution_steps.explain: child's own ways of knowing; the indispensable caring adult
match difficulty to capability so interest and motivation survive

worked_examples.q: Which psychologist showed children understand the world in their own ways: Piaget or Vygotsky?

concepts.title: Skills and Training for ECCE Professionals
concepts.definition: An early childhood worker needs genuine interest in children, knowledge of their needs and capacities, stamina for long physical activity, a repertoire of stories, songs and art skills, flexibility to drop a lesson plan mid stream, plus administrative ability for records and parent contact; entry runs through nursery teacher training, one year diplomas or a degree with child development and psychology.
concepts.formula: profile -- interest plus knowledge plus arts repertoire plus stamina plus flexibility plus administration
concepts.key_idea: Short attention spans make a large stock of ready activities and quick adaptability compulsory.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe106.txt, skills list and training routes (approx lines 390-455)
question_patterns: list the skills an ECCE worker must have
why must a preschool teacher keep a large repertoire of activities ready
which courses open the door to a career in early childhood care
why does a preschool teacher need administrative and management skills
how do arts skills like storytelling and music help an ECCE teacher
why should parents too understand individual differences between children

solution_steps.explain: interest, knowledge, interaction capacity, creativity, energy, flexibility
NTT, diploma and open university courses after school, degrees with child development for higher entry

worked_examples.q: Short attention spans make a large stock of ready what compulsory: activities or punishments?

concepts.title: Scope and Careers in ECCE
concepts.definition: Trained workers serve as nursery teachers, creche and day care caregivers, programme team members, campaign planners in government and NGOs, teacher trainers or entrepreneurs running camps, activity clubs and preschool centres, and can climb to postgraduate and doctoral study.
concepts.formula: service map -- creches plus day care plus nursery schools plus NGOs plus ICDS plus training institutes
concepts.key_idea: Entrepreneurship means setting up one's own programme at home or in separate space, which adds management expertise to teaching skill.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe106.txt, Scope, services and careers lists (approx lines 456-521)
question_patterns: name the services commonly available in early childhood care

solution_steps.explain: creches, day care centres, nursery schools, NGOs, ICDS, training institutes
teacher or caregiver to coordinator, trainer, planner, entrepreneur or researcher

worked_examples.q: Trained ECCE workers serve as nursery teachers, caregivers or what planners in NGOs: campaign or wedding?

concepts.title: Span of Developmental Stages
concepts.definition: Each developmental stage occupies a stated age band, and the width of any band in years is the upper age minus the lower age of that band.
concepts.key_idea: The toddler band covers one year, infancy one to two, and the preschool band four years from three to seven.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe106.txt, Basic concepts stage bands (approx lines 216-245)
question_patterns: the toddler stage runs from 2 to 3 years; how many years wide is this band
a programme admits children from 3 to 8 years; compute the span in years it covers
calculate the width in years of a stage that begins at birth and ends at age one
find the number of years between the start and end ages of any stated developmental band
how long in years does the phase from 3 years to 8 years last

solution_steps.action: subtract the lower age from the upper age
solution_steps.explain: the difference gives the band width in years

worked_examples.q: The toddler band covers how many years: one or ten?

concepts.title: Infancy Share of Early Childhood
concepts.definition: Since early childhood runs from birth to eight years, the one year of infancy occupies a fixed percentage of that window, found by dividing the infancy span by the whole span and scaling to one hundred.
concepts.key_idea: One year out of eight makes infancy one eighth, about 12.5 per cent, of early childhood.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe106.txt, Basic concepts stage definitions (approx lines 216-221)
question_patterns: infancy lasts 1 year and early childhood runs from birth to 8 years; what percentage of early childhood is infancy
compute the share of the birth to 8 window taken up by the first year of life
express infancy as a percentage of the full early childhood span
find what fraction in per cent one stage forms of the whole birth to eight window
what per cent of early childhood remains after infancy ends, taking infancy as 1 year

solution_steps.explain: subtract the starting age from the ending age of early childhood

solution_steps.action: divide infancy by the window and scale
solution_steps.explain: the quotient times one hundred is the percentage share

worked_examples.q: One year of infancy out of eight makes what percent of early childhood: 12.5 or 80?
